instruction: Split the employee data in column A into First Name, Last Name, and Rank. Then create a column E titled 'Full Name' with each employee's name in 'LastName, FirstName' format.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully split mixed employee data (FirstName LastName Rank) from column A into separate First Name (B), Last Name (C), and Rank (D) columns using formulas in LibreOffice Calc. Completed in 20 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc cells, enter formulas for text splitting (LEFT, MID, RIGHT, FIND), copy formulas down columns, handle multi-word parsing
metadata.explanation: Extends the text-splitting task by requiring recombination into 'LastName, FirstName' format. Getter reads columns B, C, E; metric checks header, split data, and reversed name correctness with partial credit.
metadata.task_rationale: Model proved it can split text. This variation requires splitting AND recombining in a different format, testing text concatenation skills.

scoring_breakdown.split_data: 0.3 - First name and last name columns populated

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts column E header, column E full names, and columns B/C first/last names from rows 2-22 (21 data rows matching 21 expected names)
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_full_names') without wrapping
Partial credit scoring is well-designed: 0.2 for header, 0.3 for split data presence, 0.5 proportional for name correctness
Postconfig correctly saves the file with Ctrl+S before getter reads it

Minor coverage gap: instruction requires splitting into First Name, Last Name, AND Rank, but evaluator does not verify column D (Rank). However, the main novel requirement (Full Name in reversed format) is fully verified, and correct split data in B/C implies Rank in D is likely correct too
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a check for column D (Rank) to fully verify all three split columns, not just First Name and Last Name
